title: agents --check treats any CLI version difference as drift, so --require-installed fails on version skew alone
description:
Reported via opum-agent (orchestrator brief, 2026-09-05): opum-agent's managed block was pinned at Quest 0.3.1; the installed CLI is now 0.3.2, and quest agents --check --require-installed - the CI form quest's own instructions tell projects to run - fails on that version difference alone, even though nothing else about the block changed. That failure recurs on every patch/minor bump until someone re-runs --update-instructions, which makes the CI gate fail closed on routine version drift rather than on an actual content problem.

Confirmed by direct source read: the block template embeds the currently-installed QUEST_VERSION verbatim into its prose ("This project uses Quest CLI ${QUEST_VERSION} for tracker operations.", src/application/agents/agent-instructions.ts:15-19, QUEST_VERSION from src/application/version.ts:2). checkQuestAgentInstructions (same file, lines 34-55) compares the extracted block against the freshly-built current-version block with strict string equality (`if (`${blocks[0]}\n` !== questAgentInstructions)`, line 48) - there is no semver parsing or compatibility range, so any version difference at all, even with otherwise-identical content, is reported as drift with message "Quest agent instruction block differs from version ${QUEST_VERSION}." (line 51), the same error_type as a real content change.

Scope: this is about whether/how a version-only difference should be distinguishable from a real content/shape drift for gating purposes. It does not question that missing and genuine drift should still fail.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A decision is recorded on what counts as a compatible version for the managed block (for example: same block content/shape across a patch/minor bump, or an explicit declared compatibility range) versus what should still be flagged

quest agents --check (and --require-installed) tolerates a version-only difference within the declared compatibility rule while still failing on any actual content/shape drift, OR the current strict-pin behavior is kept and explicitly documented as intentional - the decision is explicit either way, not left as an accidental side effect of string interpolation
Command help (quest help agents) and the agent-instructions guide document the chosen behavior so a caller is not surprised by which kind of mismatch gates CI

Tests cover: a same-minor-version-bump block reports the chosen outcome (current or drift, per the recorded decision), genuine content drift still reports drift, and a fully missing block still reports missing
